info.description:
## Versioning

The API is versioned using the [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/) scheme. The version number is in the format of
`v..` where:
  - `` - major version of the API. When major version is changed, backward compatibility is not guaranteed.
  - `` - minor version of the API within the given major version. There is guaranteed backward compatibility of
    minor versions of the API within one major version. Minor version is incremented when new features are added.
  - `` - patch version is increased when there are only bugfixes in new release.

You can access individual API versions using `/v` prefix, but you cannot access different minor versions.
There is also a `/latest` prefix which will always point to the latest version of the API.

### Deprecation policy

The current major version is the supported one. It is supported until the next major version is released. After next major
version is released, the previous major version is then supported for **one additional year**. After that, the previous
major version is dropped and removed and the applications must be updated to use current version of the API. After releasing
new major version, there generally won't be any additional new features added to previous major version. However, bugfixes will
be backported to the previous version too.

## Authentication & Authorization
To access the API, you need an API Access Token. To obtain the token, use the `/user/token` endpoint. That endpoint expects
refresh token, which may be generated after logging into your Sklik.cz account and creating the token in the Tools section.

When you have the access token, each call then requires `Authorization` HTTP header with `Bearer` scheme containing the obtained
access token.

The access token validity is 1 hour. The refresh token has validity you specify when creating it.

**Note:** Do not call `/user/token` endpoint prior to each API call, the endpoint is rate-limited. The intended use is to call
it once before all the processing you need to do, then reuse the token until it expires.

### Access to linked account

Each access token specifies which account it is valid for. By default, when not specifying otherwise, the token is valid for
the account that was used to create the token. However, you can specify the `user_id` parameter in the `/user/token` endpoint
to create the token for different account. Note that you need to have access to this account prior to trying to create access
token for it.

### Scopes

Access token contains authorized scopes for the user. The scopes are used to limit the access to the API. Each endpoint
defines scopes it requires to access that endpoint. You can limit scopes by scope groups when creating the refresh token.

- `r` - provides only read access
- `rw` - provides read and write access
- `rwa` - provides read and write access and also authorizes application to perform additional administrative actions
  such as linking accounts.

**Note:** On top of refresh token access level, the access level negotiated between linked accounts is considered too. So
for link with only `r` access level, `rw` refresh token will not gain you any additional authorization that would exceed the
`r` access level for that account. So generally speaking, refresh token can only narrow the scope of the token, not widen it.

You can narrow a single access token further by passing the `scope` parameter to the `/user/token` endpoint with the
access levels you want, separated by spaces. The requested access levels must be a subset of the access levels of the
refresh token you are exchanging, so the parameter can only narrow the token, never widen it; asking for more results
in `422 Unprocessable Entity`. When you leave `scope` out, the token carries all access levels of that refresh token.
The exception is the OAuth2 client-credentials grant, which has no refresh token to inherit from and therefore
defaults to read access only.

## Rate limiting

The API is rate-limited. There is a global rate limit for the API, which is shared across all endpoints. Additional rate limit
may be in place for specific endpoints, which is defined in the endpoint documentation.

Default rate limit is 5 requests per second for the API as a whole. This means that you can make up to 5 requests
per second across all endpoints. If you exceed this limit, you will receive a `429 Too Many Requests` response with
`Retry-After` header indicating how long you should wait before making another request.

Each response from the API contains the `RateLimit-Policy` and `RateLimit` header, which you can use to check the current
rate limit policy and your current usage of the rate limit. The headers are following current IETF RateLimit draft version 9,
you can find more information at the [draft](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers-09)
specification.

oneOf.description:
Model validation error. Possible types are:

- `missing`: This error is raised when a required value is missing.
- `datetime_from_date_parsing`: This error is raised when the input value is a string that cannot be parsed for a `datetime` field.
- `set_type`: This error is raised when the input value's type is not valid for a `set` field.
- `date_from_datetime_parsing`: This error is raised when the input value is a string that cannot be parsed for a date field.
- `date_past`: This error is raised when the value provided for a `PastDate` field is not in the past.
- `complex_type`: This error is raised when the input value's type is not valid for a `complex` field.
- `complex_str_parsing`: This error is raised when the input value is a string but cannot be parsed as a complex number.
- `float_type`: This error is raised when the input value's type is not valid for a `float` field.
- `iteration_error`: This error is raised when an error occurs while iterating over the input value.
- `enum`: This error is raised when the input value is not a valid `enum` member.
- `int_from_float`: This error is raised when you provide a `float` value for an `int` field.
- `bytes_invalid_encoding`: This error is raised when a `bytes` value is invalid under the configured encoding.
- `string_too_short`: This error is raised when the input value is a string whose length is less than the field's `min_length` constraint.
- `uuid_parsing`: This error is raised when the input value's type is not valid for a UUID field.
- `string_sub_type`: This error is raised when the value is an instance of a strict subtype of `str` when the field is strict.
- `assertion_error`: This error is raised when a failing `assert` statement is encountered during validation.
- `bytes_too_long`: This error is raised when a `bytes` value is longer than the configured maximum length.
- `datetime_future`: This error is raised when the input value provided for a `FutureDatetime` field is not in the future.
- `literal_error`: This error is raised when the input value is not one of the expected literals.
- `datetime_past`: This error is raised when the value provided for a `PastDatetime` field is not in the past.
- `date_parsing`: This error is raised when validating JSON where the input value is string that cannot be parsed for a date field.
- `decimal_parsing`: This error is raised when the value provided for a `Decimal` could not be parsed as a decimal number.
- `url_too_long`: This error is raised when the URL length is greater than 2083.
- `timezone_aware`: This error is raised when the `datetime` value provided for a timezone-aware `datetime` field doesn't have timezone information.

- `list_type`: This error is raised when the input value's type is not valid for a `list` field.
- `dict_type`: This error is raised when the input value's type is not valid for a `dict` field.
- `iterable_type`: This error is raised when the input value's type is not valid for an iterable field.

post.description:
Obtain access token for accessing API resources.

Supports three grant types:

- **client_credentials**: two modes share this grant type:
  - Provide an existing refresh token as a Bearer `Authorization` header to exchange
    it for an access token (use `user_id` to access a foreign account that granted
    you access). To obtain a refresh token, log in at https://www.sklik.cz/.
  - Or authenticate as an OAuth2 client (RFC 6749 §4.4) with `client_id`/`client_secret`
    supplied either via HTTP `Basic` auth or the `client_id`/`client_secret` form
    fields, to obtain a client-only access token (no refresh token). A client that is
    allowed to access any account may pass `user_id` to obtain a token acting on that
    account instead; the token's scope still comes only from the client's own roles.

- **authorization_code** (RFC 6749 §4.1.3, RFC 7636): exchange a single-use authorization
  code for an access + refresh token pair. Requires `code` and `redirect_uri`. `code_verifier`
  is required when PKCE was used during authorization.

- **refresh_token** (RFC 6749 §6): obtain a new access token from a previously issued
  refresh token passed as the `refresh_token` form field.

Pass `scope` to obtain a token narrower than the refresh token you are exchanging.

Use the access token in the `Authorization` header as a `Bearer` token.
For example: `Authorization: Bearer {access_token}`.

schema.description: Time granularity of statistics. 'total' (default) returns a single aggregate over the whole period. Any other value returns a time series: the entity is repeated once per time bucket, each row carrying that bucket's statistics and its 'firstDate' (added automatically). Requires 'statisticsDateFrom'/'statisticsDateTo'. Max 60 buckets: daily up to 1 month, weekly up to 1 year, monthly/quarterly/yearly up to 60 calendar months/quarters/years. Because the response stays flat, 'limit' and 'offset' count bucket rows, not entities - a granular listing returns fewer entities per page than 'limit' suggests, and an entity can be split across two pages. Buckets of one entity are ordered chronologically, but 'order' is applied first, so ordering by a statistic value interleaves buckets of different entities.

schema.description: Time granularity of statistics. 'total' (default) returns a single aggregate over the whole period. Any other value returns a time series: the entity is repeated once per time bucket, each row carrying that bucket's statistics and its 'firstDate' (added automatically). Requires 'statisticsDateFrom'/'statisticsDateTo'. Max 60 buckets: daily up to 1 month, weekly up to 1 year, monthly/quarterly/yearly up to 60 calendar months/quarters/years. Because the response stays flat, 'limit' and 'offset' count bucket rows, not entities - a granular listing returns fewer entities per page than 'limit' suggests, and an entity can be split across two pages. Buckets of one entity are ordered chronologically, but 'order' is applied first, so ordering by a statistic value interleaves buckets of different entities.

schema.title: Statistics Granularity
schema.description: Time granularity of statistics. 'total' (default) returns a single aggregate over the whole period. Any other value returns a time series: the entity is repeated once per time bucket, each row carrying that bucket's statistics and its 'firstDate' (added automatically). Requires 'statisticsDateFrom'/'statisticsDateTo'. Max 60 buckets: daily up to 1 month, weekly up to 1 year, monthly/quarterly/yearly up to 60 calendar months/quarters/years. Because the response stays flat, 'limit' and 'offset' count bucket rows, not entities - a granular listing returns fewer entities per page than 'limit' suggests, and an entity can be split across two pages. Buckets of one entity are ordered chronologically, but 'order' is applied first, so ordering by a statistic value interleaves buckets of different entities.

in a separate list. Creation of the Retargeting list can fail on its own, so that list can be empty
even when the conversion was created.

grant_type.title: Grant type
grant_type.description: The type of grant being used: `client_credentials`, `authorization_code`, or `refresh_token`.

user_id.title: Foreign account user ID
user_id.description:
User ID of the account to access.

When authenticating as a user (a refresh token or an authorization code), leave this empty to get a token for
yourself. To access a foreign account you must have been granted access to it beforehand; otherwise you will receive
a 403 Forbidden error.

When authenticating as an OAuth2 client (`grant_type=client_credentials` with `client_id`/`client_secret`), leave
this empty to get a token representing the client itself, which no endpoint accepts yet. Set it to obtain a token
that accesses that account instead; this is available only to clients allowed to access any account, and the request
otherwise fails with 401 Unauthorized.

scope.title: Requested access levels
scope.description:
Space-separated list of access levels the issued access token should be limited to:

- `r` - read access only
- `rw` - read and write access
- `rwa` - read and write access plus administrative actions such as linking accounts

Applies to `grant_type=refresh_token`, to a refresh token passed as a Bearer header, and to the OAuth2
client-credentials grant. With `grant_type=authorization_code` the tokens always carry the access levels the
account owner approved on the authorization page, so the field has no effect there.

The scope can only be narrowed, never widened: it must be a subset of the access levels of the refresh token you
are exchanging. Requesting a level you were not granted fails with `422 Unprocessable Entity`. The refresh token
itself is never narrowed, so a later call can request its full scope again.

When left empty, the token carries every access level of the refresh token. The one exception is authenticating as
an OAuth2 client (`grant_type=client_credentials` with `client_id`/`client_secret`): there is no refresh token to
inherit from, so an empty scope means read access only (`r`) and write or administrative access has to be
requested explicitly.

redirect_uri.description: Required when grant_type=authorization_code. Must exactly match the URI used during authorization.
